name: Shadows of the Custodian
throughline_question: When the friend you trust is also the betrayer you need to stop, when the institution has not earned the loyalty it asks for, and when the life you came from is still offering you a place to land â€” what does belonging actually mean, and what are you willing to lose to claim it?

core_party.name: Clovis Beryl
core_party.table_function: Player lens. Every party bond should clarify what belonging costs Clovis, not replace his choice.
core_party.player_facing_question: Can I be known by one true name and still survive?
core_party.primary_payoff: Clovis's ending identity is defined by which people he lets matter before the war-temple.

core_party.name: Joran Veska
core_party.table_function: Make the player care before suspicion becomes fair. His warmth is real; his mission is real.
core_party.player_facing_question: Can the friend who betrays me still be someone I try to save?
core_party.primary_payoff: His bond state is the primary lever for Open Door, Long Road, The Law, and What Remains.

core_party.name: Rann Veska
core_party.table_function: Checks hope against facts. She should make secrets harder to keep without feeling like a quest marker.
core_party.player_facing_question: Can hope survive being checked against the facts?
core_party.primary_payoff: Her trust defines whether the Third Path feels chosen, desperate, or impossible.

core_party.name: Tarsh Voll
core_party.table_function: Gives Clovis the first peer who feels like old life without pulling him backward.
core_party.relationship_axis: usefulness versus being loved without work
core_party.player_facing_question: Can someone like us belong here without becoming polished first?
core_party.primary_payoff: High bond makes the Horizon, academy infrastructure, and early belonging feel earned.

core_party.name: Brann Riako
core_party.table_function: Turns old Imperial pattern-reading into protection, then asks what that protection costs.
core_party.relationship_axis: Imperial pattern recognition used for protection
core_party.player_facing_question: Can old Imperial habits be used to save people the Empire would have discarded?
core_party.primary_payoff: His Act 4 cost lands as witnessed sacrifice or lonely consequence.

core_party.name: Cassen Vell
core_party.table_function: Shows whether status becomes extraction, cover, or chosen service.
core_party.player_facing_question: Can privilege become protection instead of extraction?
core_party.primary_payoff: His refusal of family extraction shows the academy becoming a real home.

core_party.name: Inya Vorn
core_party.table_function: Makes combat personal by asking whether inherited form can become chosen restraint.
core_party.player_facing_question: Is discipline what was given to me, or what I choose under pressure?
core_party.primary_payoff: Her bond affects who survives the Drel/Sona combat layer in Act 5.

core_party.name: Lirah Tann
core_party.table_function: Keeps the party human when triage, resentment, and duty collide.
core_party.player_facing_question: Can a calling count if I am still angry about what it cost?
core_party.primary_payoff: Her bond determines whether triage in Acts 4-5 becomes collapse, competence, or grace.

supporting_cast_tiers.purpose: The recurring social-RPG party. These characters receive priority in ordinary-life scenes, bond slots, and Act 5 payoff.
Optional social-link characters who add depth without needing equal screen time each playthrough.
Authority, instruction, and Legends texture. Use them when their function matters; do not let canon guests solve Clovis's story.
Opposition pressure. Each antagonist should test a specific party value rather than simply increase danger.

bond_act_plan.pacing_note: Slowest act. Prioritize first impressions, ordinary life, and one clear chosen peer bond.
Investigation act. Let the player choose who becomes their practical party before suspicion hardens.
Midpoint rupture. Social time narrows because the Joran truth must dominate.
Consequence act. Bonds should pay off under stress rather than introduce many new threads.
Final act. One last chosen conversation, then payoff. No new social arcs.

bond_pacing_matrix.policy: Keep the full bond library as authored material, but surface only required story bonds and a small priority pool by default. Optional and rare bonds should require clear player drift, prior attention, or a directly relevant scene context. A typical playthrough should feel curated, not completionist.
bond_pacing_matrix.no_cut_reason: No bond event is a hard cut yet. The library is large but every event now has a clear function, payoff, and route value. Pruning should happen at runtime offer priority rather than deleting authored routes.

act_plans.guidance: Act 1 should breathe, but not scatter. Always build Joran. Then give the player one warm peer path and one chosen curiosity path.
Act 2 has the greatest offer pressure. Default to Joran, Brann, and one player-selected companion. Do not let side links delay the investigation.
Act 3 belongs to the Joran rupture. Other bonds should either clarify that rupture or help the player process it.
Act 4 should pay off what the player already chose. Avoid opening fresh emotional lanes unless the player has been asking for them.
Act 5 gets one last chosen conversation. Post-fight tags can appear only if they directly close a route the player clearly invested in.

group_scenes.title: First Dinner
group_scenes.hook: The welcome meal and meal-share ritual. Tarsh saves Clovis a seat, Joran is easy company, Rann watches too carefully, and the cohort becomes more than names.
group_scenes.function: Establish party texture and first impressions before the mystery takes over.

group_scenes.title: Archive Chore Day
group_scenes.hook: A routine archive chore puts Clovis near Rann's vigilance, Olm's preserved gestures, Tionne's restricted archive crate, and Joran's too-useful calm.
group_scenes.function: Make lore texture social instead of expositional, with Lore/Perception/Sense cues available if the player presses the restricted crate or Olm's gesture.

group_scenes.title: Training Rotation
group_scenes.hook: A rotating practical drill pairs students who do not normally choose each other. Competence, class habits, and anger all show in motion.
group_scenes.function: Show the party as playable combat/social units and surface mechanical identities.

group_scenes.title: Post-Wound Medbay
group_scenes.hook: After Iila is wounded, the medbay becomes the cohort's first shared room of fear. Lirah holds steady, Tarsh wants to fix something, and Brann notices who cannot look at the door.
group_scenes.function: Make danger personal and convert plot threat into party care.

group_scenes.title: Dormitory Argument
group_scenes.hook: Suspicion makes ordinary living impossible. A dormitory argument about safety, privilege, and secrecy leaves everyone more honest than they meant to be.
group_scenes.function: Narrow the social field before the Joran reveal and clarify who trusts whom.

group_scenes.title: Mission Briefing
group_scenes.hook: After the holocron crisis, the briefing table is no longer theoretical. The party chooses roles while the adults realize the students are already carrying the campaign.
group_scenes.function: Convert accumulated bonds into tactical roles for the heist aftermath and Maradun preparation.

group_scenes.title: Breach Aftermath
group_scenes.hook: The academy damage leaves everyone doing small practical work: lights, water, transport, triage, family calls, and the first private admission that nobody feels ready.
group_scenes.function: Let bonds pay off through care work before the final mission narrows the story.

group_scenes.title: Final Hyperspace Lull
group_scenes.hook: On the jump to the Maradun expanse, there is time for one last chosen conversation. Everyone knows it may decide what they can survive becoming.
group_scenes.function: Give the player one final social choice before the ending locks.

ending_payoff_matrix.title: Open Door
requires: High Joran bond or planted doubt
Clovis stands with the academy without abandoning old family

relationship_payoffs.Joran Veska: Joran turns at the climax because doubt has been loved into him, not argued into him.
relationship_payoffs.Rann Veska: Rann receives a living answer to her hope and must decide how to forgive slowly.
relationship_payoffs.Tarsh Voll: Tarsh and the Horizon make the rescue infrastructure feel earned.
relationship_payoffs.Brann Riako: If Brann died, his pattern work is named as the reason the door stayed open.

ending_payoff_matrix.emotional_contract: The player earned hope, but not a clean slate.
ending_payoff_matrix.future_hook: Karrde calls his favor later, and Joran's recovery remains a long, playable consequence.
ending_payoff_matrix.avoid_feeling: Do not make Joran instantly healed or the academy instantly vindicated.

ending_payoff_matrix.title: Long Road
requires: Joran sabotages the Custodian but disappears
Trust with Joran exists but did not fully convert him

relationship_payoffs.Joran Veska: Joran chooses not to complete the mission but cannot yet choose the academy.
relationship_payoffs.Rann Veska: Rann has a direction to follow and a reason not to collapse.
relationship_payoffs.Tarsh Voll: Tarsh's bond turns the Horizon into the ship that can keep looking.
relationship_payoffs.Brann Riako: Brann's evidence trail gives the search shape after the credits.

ending_payoff_matrix.emotional_contract: The story ends decisively by choosing the search, not by solving it.
ending_payoff_matrix.future_hook: The next campaign can follow Karrde-network leads, Joran sightings, and Vornn's wound.
ending_payoff_matrix.avoid_feeling: Do not frame disappearance as failure if the player built trust.

ending_payoff_matrix.title: The Law
requires: Joran captured or handed to Luke early

relationship_payoffs.Joran Veska: Joran is stopped before he can choose, so safety is real and grief is unresolved.
relationship_payoffs.Rann Veska: Rann does not forgive the speed or secrecy of the decision.
relationship_payoffs.Tarsh Voll: Tarsh helps keep the academy functioning but cannot soften the emotional result.
relationship_payoffs.Brann Riako: Brann's caution is vindicated, which should feel useful and sad.

ending_payoff_matrix.emotional_contract: The player saved people by choosing authority, and someone they love pays emotionally for that.
ending_payoff_matrix.future_hook: Joran's custody, Rann's distance, and Luke's institutional choices can all echo later.
ending_payoff_matrix.avoid_feeling: Do not punish the player with disaster; the cost is relational, not plot failure.

ending_payoff_matrix.title: Third Path
requires: Cohort losses or academy rupture are accepted costs

relationship_payoffs.Joran Veska: Joran's fate matters, but Rann becomes the living choice in front of Clovis.
relationship_payoffs.Rann Veska: Rann is chosen without being made into a reward.
relationship_payoffs.Tarsh Voll: Tarsh's hurt should register because Clovis leaves people who had become real.
relationship_payoffs.Brann Riako: If Brann's cost has landed, this ending knows exactly what protection can cost.

ending_payoff_matrix.emotional_contract: The player ends the story by choosing a person over an institution, with eyes open.
ending_payoff_matrix.future_hook: Karrde's network absorbs Clovis and Rann, opening a fugitive/fringe Jedi thread.
ending_payoff_matrix.avoid_feeling: Do not romanticize abandonment; make the saved person and the people left behind both matter.

ending_payoff_matrix.title: What Remains
requires: Low commitment or contradictory final choices

relationship_payoffs.Joran Veska: Joran remains unresolved because Clovis never forced the relationship into truth.
relationship_payoffs.Rann Veska: Rann survives with unanswered verification or is lost to the consequence web.
relationship_payoffs.Tarsh Voll: Tarsh's warmth becomes the measure of what was not protected.
relationship_payoffs.Brann Riako: Brann's warning stands as the thing the story did not heed in time.

ending_payoff_matrix.emotional_contract: This is not a joke ending; it is the coherent result of drift under pressure.
ending_payoff_matrix.future_hook: Vornn, partial Massassi awakening, and unresolved Joran state become future scars.
ending_payoff_matrix.avoid_feeling: Do not make this feel random or scolding. It should feel causally earned.

allegiances.description: Students of Luke Skywalker's five-year-old Jedi Praxeum on Yavin 4, learning to wield the Force in a galaxy that has consolidated around the New Republic but has not yet decided what relationship the Jedi should have to civilian authority. The institution is past its founding-fragility and into the harder phase of discovering its own compromises.

character_variants.selection_note: Intended protagonist for Shadows of the Custodian. Use this route for canonical play.
character_variants.pitch: Clovis Beryl, a human Sentinel/Shadow in his early twenties, survived an Imperial execution order because the smuggler crew of the Glass Wake pulled him out through the cracks. Now he has been called to Luke Skywalker's Praxeum, five years into its life, and is leaving the only family he has known to learn whether trust can be a discipline rather than a vulnerability.
character_variants.starting_situation: Aboard the Glass Wake at a fringe shadowport, the night before departure for Yavin 4. The crew has prepared the wrong stew for goodbye dinner. Captain Tev has the encrypted contact codes ready and is waiting for Clovis to name a recipient. The Praxeum's supply shuttle Horizon arrives at first light. Clovis has not yet asked himself what he is losing â€” until a quiet visitor arrives during dinner who asks him exactly that.
character_variants.voice_baseline: Guarded, dry, observant. Speaks like someone editing himself in real time. Uses smuggler slang when startled or comfortable, then notices he has done it. Polite with teachers, quietly funny with peers, ruthless about exits and contingencies.
character_variants.background: A human from a Mid Rim trade family scheduled for execution by the Empire after their shipping accounts were used to move fugitives. The smuggler crew of the Glass Wake â€” Captain Tev and his people â€” saved Clovis as a child and raised him among cargo holds, false manifests, and customs lies. His Force sensitivity first appeared as impossible timing and danger sense. Talon Karrde noticed before Luke Skywalker did. The Praxeum is the first place asking Clovis to survive by trusting instead of hiding â€” and Karrde has not stopped watching to see whether it works.

integration_layer.entry_point: Clovis arrives at the Praxeum on the supply shuttle Horizon, in the same arrival cohort as Joran Veska. The academy is five years old, institutionally maturing, politically watched, and still haunted by what the Exar Kun crisis proved about Yavin 4. Clovis is older than the average new initiate and more guarded than the curriculum is built for.
integration_layer.personal_stakes: If Clovis cuts cleanly from the Glass Wake, he loses the only family he has known. If he keeps the door open with Karrde, he risks being claimed by the life he is trying to leave. If he fails to read Joran in time, he loses the first friend the academy gave him â€” and possibly the academy itself.

Joran Veska.relationship: fellow new arrival; first easy friendship at the academy

Rann Veska.relationship: wary cohort senior; the first person Clovis sees react to something

Tarsh Voll.relationship: fellow late-Force-bloomer who recognized Clovis as one of his own at first dinner

Luke Skywalker.relationship: teacher who is asking Clovis to trust an institution Clovis has never trusted

Tionne.relationship: intake interviewer; has read Clovis's file and asked the question Clovis is still answering

Captain Tev.relationship: de facto father; the goodbye is unfinished

Talon Karrde.relationship: patient observer; asked one question on departure night and is waiting for the answer

anchor_adaptations.arrivals: Says goodbye to the Glass Wake crew, fields Karrde's quiet visit, names a contact-code recipient, boards the Horizon. Meets Joran on the descent. Witnesses Rann's reaction in the colonnade. Settles into routine. Brann recognizes Inquisitor cell tactics on perimeter watch and pulls Clovis into the conspiracy.
anchor_adaptations.long_watch: Investigates with Brann. First offworld errand follows the cell's signature. First saber engagements with junior operatives â€” Inya is wounded. Cohort fractures politically. Joran 'helps' the investigation while quietly slowing it.
anchor_adaptations.two_brothers: Off-world mission with Kyle Katarn â€” first inconclusive duel with Drel Vass. Returning, the pieces fit. Joran is exposed. Confrontation in the lower Massassi corridors becomes a duel becomes a doubt.
anchor_adaptations.custodians_hand: Cohort survives the heist's aftermath. Holocron fragment lost or moved depending on Joran's posture. Clovis returns to the Glass Wake â€” Tev â€” then Karrde. Field log secured. Mara dispatched. Brann's last stand at the perimeter.
anchor_adaptations.what_remains: War-temple in the Maradun expanse. Role depends on Joran's status. Multiple parallel battles. Final confrontation with Joran â€” the seed planted in Act 3 either blooms or does not.

starting_force_powers.name: Sense
starting_force_powers.narrative_capability: Can sense the emotions and immediate intentions of nearby beings. For Clovis, this often arrives as a survival instinct before it feels like a sacred discipline.
starting_force_powers.gm_choice_guidance: Offer sensing choices when Clovis could read fear, notice a lie, feel danger before it becomes visible, or distinguish genuine trust from practiced misdirection. Especially relevant around Joran, Luke's trust exercises, and the lower Massassi corridors.
starting_force_powers.dark_side_flavor: Dark side Sense feels like casing a room by tearing the truth out of everyone in it.

character_variants.protagonist_contradiction: Believes secrecy saves lives, but the Jedi path keeps asking him to trust people before he has proof they deserve it.
character_variants.pressure_revealed_identity: Under maximum pressure, Clovis becomes the person who stays visible so someone else can make it out alive.
character_variants.contradiction_origin: The Glass Wake saved Clovis by lying, hiding, and moving faster than Imperial truth. His family died because public law called them criminals. Trusting authority feels less like wisdom than forgetting the lesson that kept him breathing.

depth_card.inner_demon: Fear that survival has made him unfit for peace â€” too suspicious, too ready to lie, too comfortable in shadows.
depth_card.secret_yearning: To be known by one true name and not regret it.
depth_card.lesson_not_learned: That trust is not the absence of caution. It is choosing what caution serves.
depth_card.worst_act: Let a frightened informant take the blame for a smuggling run because correcting the story would have exposed the Glass Wake. The informant survived prison, but Clovis never checked what it cost them.
depth_card.social_mask: The useful newcomer: polite, competent, funny enough to deflect questions, always willing to take the errand that lets him learn the building.
depth_card.under_pressure: Goes quiet, gathers leverage, makes contingency plans, and withholds the one detail someone else most needs.
depth_card.worldview: Institutions say protection and mean control. People say trust and mean leverage. The Force may be different, but he needs evidence.
depth_card.moral_line: Will not hand a vulnerable person to power simply because power asks cleanly.

narrative_arc.lie: Trust is what gets you killed. The world is full of people who pretend to be safe and turn out not to be. Survival means keeping your real self in the back room of every conversation, and the Force is just one more skill to keep there.
narrative_arc.ghost: His family died because they trusted that legal process would protect them when their shipping accounts were misused. Public law called them criminals before any court did. The Glass Wake saved him at twelve by teaching him to never be findable. He has not stopped checking exits since.
narrative_arc.truth: Trust is not the absence of caution. It is choosing what caution serves. The Glass Wake taught him to survive; the academy is asking him to live. Both can be true. Both require an honesty he was not capable of when he arrived.
narrative_arc.want: To find a place that holds his real self without demanding he stop being the kid who got out by lying. To make the Praxeum that place, if he can. To make the Glass Wake still be that place too, if he must.
narrative_arc.need: To stop performing competence for the people who already love him. To risk being known by one true name.

party_dossier.rpg_function: Player lens for belonging under pressure; every bond should clarify what caution serves.
party_dossier.act1_player_feel: Competent, funny, guarded, and visibly homesick once the Glass Wake falls behind him.

social_bond_arc.act1: Chooses how much of his old self the cohort is allowed to see.
social_bond_arc.act2: Learns that investigation requires trust as much as suspicion.
social_bond_arc.act3: Has to decide what love does when a friend is also evidence.
social_bond_arc.act4: Returns to the Wake and Karrde with new loyalties, not clean loyalties.
social_bond_arc.act5: Makes one visible choice that defines where he belongs.

party_dossier.utility: Sentinel/Shadow play: stealth, perception, underworld instincts, danger sense, and moral triage.
party_dossier.best_case_ending_payoff: Becomes a Jedi who keeps the door open to the Wake without being owned by it.
party_dossier.worst_case_ending_payoff: Survives by withholding too much, leaving Joran, Rann, or the cohort to carry the cost.
party_dossier.avoid: Do not make him a blank-slate hero or a clean Jedi convert. His old family stays real.

allegiances.description: Late-Force-bloomers and fringe-recruited Padawans whose path to the Praxeum did not run through the canonical New Republic channels. They arrive older, scarred, and useful in ways the academy has not yet figured out how to use.

The Whetstone crew sent him to the Praxeum partly out of love and partly because they were afraid of him.

integration_layer.personal_stakes: If Tarsh fails to keep the discipline holding, he hurts someone the academy loves. If the academy fails, he has nowhere to go that is not afraid of him.

acts.name: Arrivals
acts.opening_situation: Aboard the Glass Wake, dockside at a fringe shadowport, the night before Clovis Beryl departs for Yavin 4. The freighter's main hold has been cleared for a goodbye meal that nobody is calling a goodbye meal. Three people share the table with him. Mira, the cook who has been on the Wake since Clovis was twelve, the one who learned at thirteen that he hated her cumin-sharp Karkaron stew and has cooked it on every birthday, every bad night, every farewell since, sets the wrong stew down with a flat face that says she will be fine and not to mention it. Renn, older brother in everything but blood, the one who taught Clovis how to walk past a customs queue without looking at the floor and how to lie about a name without flinching, leans in the doorway with a bottle of something illegal he produced from inside his jacket. He is making jokes about whether the Jedi let you keep your own haircut. Across the table sits Captain Tev, Corellian, late fifties, the man who pulled Clovis out of a bonded cargo chute six hours before the Imperial executions began and has been the closest thing to a father he has known since. Tev has the encrypted contact codes for the Wake's emergency network folded in his coat pocket. He has not put them on the table yet. He will, before morning. The Praxeum's supply shuttle Horizon arrives at first light, three hours from now. The opening stretch should BREATHE. This is the goodbye scene, not the inciting incident. Lean into smuggler-life-loss: the crew ribbing Clovis about respectable haircuts, jokes about Jedi celibacy that land different tonight, Mira refusing to admit the stew is on purpose, Renn telling a story about a job that went sideways and Clovis remembering how it really went. Tev's quiet authority anchors the room without filling it. The Glass Wake transponder tag in Clovis's pocket is the Wake's encrypted emergency beacon, a one-burst call for help if things go wrong on Yavin. It is a tool, not a thematic talisman. Do not have the prose dwell on it as warmth, memory, or identity. INTRODUCTIONS: Mira, Renn, and Tev are characters the player has not met yet. Introduce them through Clovis's inner voice on first appearance: short, embedded, in motion. Not exposition paragraphs. A line about who Mira was to him at thirteen as she sets the bowl down. A beat about Renn's posture as he leans in the doorway. A specific memory of Tev that lands the moment Tev does something small. After first introduction, drop the inner voice and let them act. Karrde does NOT appear on the Wake. He arrives later in the act, at the Praxeum, dropping off a supply shipment Tionne ordered, possibly using it as cover to see Mara Jade. Clovis encounters him in passing in the colonnade, and Karrde recognizes him from his network's intelligence chain. After the goodbye and the contact-code choice (which Tev offers gently, without pressing), the Horizon arrival, the descent toward Yavin Prime, the green canopy, the Great Temple, the intake interview with Tionne, the first dinner, the meal-share ritual, the third meditation note half a tone flat. The cohort forms by accretion: Tarsh recognizes Clovis at first dinner; Joran shares the descent; Rann reacts in the colonnade to seeing Joran walk off the shuttle. Daily life takes hold over weeks: chores, archive errands, training drills, perimeter-lantern duty at dusk. The first cracks are small: a coded chip in a ration crate, a corridor someone was not in, a sparring slip Kam Solusar files silently, an old man named Streen passing through the colonnade saying 'two breaths in one chest.' By the end of the act, a perimeter scout has ambushed Brann Riako, and Brann pulls Clovis into a conspiracy he cannot yet name.
acts.opening_location: Glass Wake freighter, fringe shadowport (player's prior life)
acts.galactic_context: 16 ABY. The New Republic is twelve years old and increasingly bureaucratic. Pellaeon has consolidated much of the Imperial Remnant into a disciplined Outer Rim power, but the 19 ABY treaty is still three years away. Luke Skywalker's Praxeum at Yavin 4 is five years old, with thirty students, a small senior staff (Kam Solusar, Cilghal, Streen, Tionne, Kyle Katarn), and the political attention of a Senate oversight coalition led by Senator Karro. The Disciples of Ragnos crisis is two years past; Tavion's surviving disciples are dispersed but not extinct. Brakiss is operating quietly in the Outer Rim. Talon Karrde's information network is the closest thing the post-war fringe has to a clearing house.
open_threads: What was Karrde's question, and what would Clovis answer if he had to answer now?
Who at the academy sees through Clovis's smuggler-trained cover most accurately?
What is wrong with Joran that Rann sees and the cohort doesn't?
What did Streen mean by 'two breaths in one chest'?
Why does Tionne pull her hand back from the restricted archive crate?
Whose face will Brann recognize when the cell shows up in person?

xp_bonus_conditions.description: Engaged meaningfully with the academy arrival and orientation
Used at least 3 different skills during the act

milestone_windows.description: First talent purchase after establishing character approach

side_content.title: Mira's wrong stew
side_content.hook: Mira has cooked the Karkaron stew Clovis hated as a child. She does not mention she remembers. The room is laughing too loudly because everyone knows this is goodbye.
side_content.rpg_function: Establish the old family as living people, not backstory.
side_content.player_choice: Eat it, joke about it, refuse it, or admit why the gesture lands.
side_content.payoff_or_change: Sets Clovis's first emotional posture: deflective, grateful, evasive, or openly attached.

side_content.title: Karrde at the Praxeum
side_content.hook: A few days into Clovis's Praxeum life, Karrde lands at the Great Temple's lower pad with a supply shipment Tionne ordered (rare bound texts and a sensor calibrator). He is also there to see Mara Jade between her assignments. While Tionne signs for the crates, Karrde finds Clovis in the colonnade and stops for a brief, deliberate exchange. He does not lecture. He does not make demands. He notes that the Wake's young pickup grew up well, and asks one quiet question: 'Do you know what you are losing?' Then he goes.
side_content.rpg_function: Establish Karrde as a recurring fringe presence in Clovis's Praxeum life. Make the smuggler world feel like it is still watching, still a door he can step back through if he chooses. Frame Karrde as an interested observer, not a recruiter.
side_content.player_choice: Answer Karrde honestly, perform confidence, challenge the premise, or ask what he thinks Clovis is gaining. Optionally: ask after Mara Jade, after Tev, after the Wake's current run.
side_content.payoff_or_change: Karrde files the answer and calibrates his later Act 4 price around it. Disposition delta tracks against his eventual willingness to extend a favor.

side_content.title: The contact-code choice
side_content.hook: Tev gives Clovis the encrypted contact codes for the Wake's emergency network and asks who gets them if Clovis doesn't come back. The choice echoes hard in Act 4.
side_content.rpg_function: Turn old family loyalty into a mechanical-seeming promise before the academy appears; Deception, Streetwise, or Negotiation can change how cleanly Tev accepts the plan.
side_content.player_choice: Name a recipient, refuse to plan for failure, keep the codes private, or give Tev a condition.
side_content.payoff_or_change: Defines who can reach the Wake when Act 4 collapses into rescue logistics.

side_content.title: Joran on the descent
side_content.hook: Aboard the Horizon during the Yavin 4 descent, Joran Veska sits beside Clovis because the only other open seat is under a rattling conduit. He notices the old blaster-callus on Clovis's hand and asks where he learned to brace like that.
side_content.rpg_function: Make Joran likable through attention and practical kindness before he is suspicious; Perception/Sense can notice trained observation without naming betrayal.
side_content.player_choice: Tell the truth, give a smuggler half-answer, joke, or ask Joran the same question.
side_content.payoff_or_change: Creates Joran's first real friendship hook and gives the later betrayal something warm to damage.

side_content.title: Tionne's question
side_content.hook: The intake interview is brief and not what it seems. Tionne asks one question that depends on the farewell: what Clovis brought with him that the academy has no right to take.
side_content.rpg_function: Make the Praxeum feel humane but porous: it listens before it protects; Discipline or Cool can decide how much old-life truth Clovis gives away.
side_content.player_choice: Name the Wake, a skill, a fear, a debt, or nothing at all.
side_content.payoff_or_change: Tionne becomes a quiet witness to Clovis's old-life attachment and later reads him more accurately.

side_content.title: Rann in the colonnade
side_content.hook: Walking back from the intake interview, Clovis passes through the colonnade. Rann Veska is watching the new arrivals' shuttle leave. She sees Joran laughing with another student, and her face becomes hope before discipline can stop it.
side_content.rpg_function: Make Rann observant and wounded, not cryptic for its own sake.
side_content.player_choice: Acknowledge what he saw, give her privacy, ask Joran later, or file the moment silently.
side_content.payoff_or_change: Positions Clovis as Rann's possible witness before he understands what he witnessed.

side_content.title: The meal-share ritual
side_content.hook: At the welcome meal, each person names one small thing they were grateful for that day. Tarsh Voll has saved Clovis the seat next to him and greets him in spacer slang before anyone can make the table ceremonial.
side_content.rpg_function: Turn the cohort into a table the player wants to return to.
side_content.player_choice: Choose what gratitude Clovis offers and whether to meet Tarsh's warmth, dodge it, or test it.
side_content.payoff_or_change: Establishes Tarsh as easy belonging and Joran as comfortable company while Rann watches too carefully.

side_content.title: The third note half a tone flat
side_content.hook: At dusk, Clovis sits with the cohort on the upper terrace for the first meditation chime. The third note is deliberately half a tone flat - Luke's tuning, meant to keep students from mistaking peace for prettiness. Joran finds Clovis in the corridor after.
side_content.rpg_function: Introduce Jedi practice as strange, practical, and personal rather than generic mysticism.
side_content.player_choice: Admit the exercise irritated him, pretend it worked, ask about the flat note, or invite Joran to walk.
side_content.payoff_or_change: Creates the lane into Joran's late-sweep bond and shows Luke's Praxeum has local traditions.

side_content.title: An archive errand with Olm
side_content.hook: Tionne sends Clovis and Olm to retrieve a manuscript from the archive's lower shelves. Olm does a small hand-gesture before opening the sealed cabinet, casual as breathing. Tionne sees it and goes still for half a second.
side_content.rpg_function: Deliver Old Republic/Order 66 texture through work, not lecture; Lore can identify the gesture's age while Discipline decides whether Clovis presses.
side_content.player_choice: Ask Olm about the gesture, ask Tionne later, remember without pressing, or ignore the oddity.
side_content.payoff_or_change: Sets up Olm's preserved tradition and Tionne's fear of what the archives still contain.

side_content.title: Perimeter-lantern duty at dusk
side_content.hook: Clovis is assigned to walk the perimeter at dusk and light the carved glow-lanterns. Each lantern bears a student's mark, and the older students can tell who carved which line by touch.
side_content.rpg_function: Make the academy feel lived-in before the perimeter becomes dangerous.
side_content.player_choice: Carve a mark, refuse the permanence, ask whose marks are missing, or treat it as a patrol.
side_content.payoff_or_change: The same perimeter later becomes Brann's ambush site, changing a peaceful ritual into a threat.

side_content.title: First sparring with Kam Solusar
side_content.hook: Clovis's first formal saber lesson with Kam is less graceful than the brochure version. Kam corrects his stance once and watches the smuggler-tricks resolve in real time. He says nothing in front of the class.
side_content.rpg_function: Surface Clovis's practical RPG skill identity and contrast it with formal Jedi training.
side_content.player_choice: Lean into improvisation, try to conform, joke through embarrassment, or ask Kam for private correction.
side_content.payoff_or_change: Kam notices Clovis's survival training and becomes a credible adult observer when Joran's form later slips.

side_content.title: A coded chip in a ration crate
side_content.hook: During ration unloading, Clovis sees Rann find a coded chip taped beneath a crate seam. She pockets it, shows it to no one, and notices Clovis noticing before either of them can pretend otherwise.
side_content.rpg_function: Give Rann agency as an investigator before the plot explains her history.
side_content.player_choice: Confront her, offer help, quietly cover for her, or tell an adult.
side_content.payoff_or_change: Determines whether Rann sees Clovis as a witness, obstacle, or possible accomplice.

side_content.title: Joran where he wasn't
side_content.hook: A small inconsistency: Joran says he was in the archive during second bell, but Tionne is certain he was not, and Tarsh swears Joran helped him carry coolant at the same time. It is small, deniable, and easy to protect.
side_content.rpg_function: Let the player choose whether affection edits evidence.
side_content.player_choice: Ask Joran directly, check the archive log, let it go, or mention it to Rann.
side_content.payoff_or_change: The first Joran suspicion can become trust, denial, or a private note the player carries into Act 3.

side_content.title: Kam Solusar's eyes narrow
side_content.hook: During a sparring drill, Joran's footwork resolves into a defensive angle too trained to be accidental. Kam Solusar's eyes narrow, then soften before the younger students can see it.
side_content.rpg_function: Make Joran's competence attractive and suspect at the same time.
side_content.player_choice: Admire the move, ask Joran to teach it, ask Kam what he saw, or compare it against Clovis's instincts.
side_content.payoff_or_change: Creates a fair-play clue that Joran has training he should not have.

side_content.title: Streen passes through the colonnade
side_content.hook: Streen, who almost never leaves the high tower, passes through the colonnade at midday. He stops when he sees Clovis and says, 'Two breaths in one chest. The wind has been telling me. I do not know whose.' Then he leaves before anyone can make it useful.
side_content.rpg_function: Use Legends-era Praxeum weirdness as pressure, not exposition.
side_content.player_choice: Follow Streen, ask Luke, dismiss it as tower talk, or connect it to Joran/Rann.
side_content.payoff_or_change: Adds Force unease without answering whether the warning points to Joran, Rann, or Clovis.

side_content.title: Tionne's hand on the crate
side_content.hook: Late in the act, Clovis sees Tionne in the archive at dusk. She lays her hand on a quarantined crate behind the second column of cabinets without thinking, then pulls back as if the wood remembered her.
side_content.rpg_function: Place the Sadow-line holocron fragment in emotional space before it becomes plot machinery; Lore/Sense can read danger, while Threat should cost trust or strain.
side_content.player_choice: Ask directly, offer to leave, mark the crate's location, or pretend he saw nothing.
side_content.payoff_or_change: Tionne's fear of completing the translation becomes legible, and the archive stops being a neutral safe room.

side_content.title: Iila offers her ration bar
side_content.hook: Iila Vand finds Clovis somewhere he looks unsettled and offers her ration bar. She does not eat it. She offers it. The offer is the comfort, not the bar.
side_content.rpg_function: Show that not every supporting character needs a large arc to matter.
side_content.player_choice: Take the bar, refuse gently, ask why she noticed, or give her something back.
side_content.payoff_or_change: Makes Iila's Act 2 wound personal if the player accepted her kindness.

side_content.title: Kyle Katarn's field note
side_content.hook: Tionne has a short recorded field note from Kyle Katarn waiting in the training archive: practical Force application, no mysticism, no patience for pretending fear is not data. Clovis recognizes the tone before meeting the man.
side_content.rpg_function: Keep Kyle in the 16 ABY weather without bringing him onstage too early.
side_content.player_choice: Request the full module, dismiss it as mercenary thinking, ask Tionne why she saved it, or practice from the note.
side_content.payoff_or_change: Prepares Kyle's Act 2 usefulness while keeping Act 1 centered on the cohort.

side_content.title: Brann's perimeter ambush
side_content.hook: At the end of the act, a scout ambushes Brann Riako on perimeter watch. Brann survives, wounded and controlled in the way frightened soldiers get controlled. He recognizes the operational signature: Inquisitor cell tactics.
side_content.rpg_function: Convert academy texture into danger and pull Clovis into investigation through a peer, not a council briefing.
side_content.player_choice: Help Brann hide the panic, push for Luke immediately, inspect the ambush site, or ask why Brann recognizes it.
side_content.payoff_or_change: Launches Act 2 and makes Brann's Imperial pattern-reading useful before it becomes costly.

acts.name: The Long Watch
acts.opening_situation: The night after Brann's perimeter ambush. Clovis has agreed to help him investigate quietly. Luke must be told eventually, but neither of them has enough yet, and Tionne is unwilling to alarm the Senate visitors who arrive next week. The investigation begins as comm-log review, surveillance of the perimeter, and quiet questions to support staff. Joran offers to help â€” eagerly, warmly, in ways that read (to Clovis) as genuine friendship and (to Brann, quietly) as the right kind of help offered too quickly. Off-world, the Custodian's cell sends a second probe; this one is met by an off-world cohort errand that turns into the first real saber engagement. Inya Vorn takes a wound. Tarsh wants action. Cassen worries about reputational damage. Vesh argues the academy is overreacting. The cohort fractures politically while bonding personally. Mid-act, an attempted snatch of a younger student during perimeter rotation ends with Iila Vand wounded and a saber-operative dead. The threat is now visceral. Suspicions form, and form wrongly: Cassen's family holocomms look incriminating, and Vesh's senate-coalition mother makes Vesh look ideologically motivated. By the end of the act, the protagonist is preparing for an off-world mission with Kyle Katarn to chase a deeper lead â€” and Joran has volunteered to come along.
acts.opening_location: Jedi Praxeum, perimeter watch hut and dormitory wing, Yavin 4 â€” pre-dawn
acts.galactic_context: Senate oversight pressure intensifies. Senator Karro's coalition has scheduled a hearing on the Praxeum's autonomy for late next month. Pellaeon's faction is still hostile to the New Republic, but disciplined enough that unexplained Sith-adjacent operations do not look like official Remnant policy. Karrde's Wild Karrde is in the Tion Cluster region. Mara Jade is operating semi-independently of him on a long-term assignment.

side_content.title: Comm log review with Brann
side_content.hook: Hours over a datapad in the perimeter watch hut. Brann teaches Clovis to read Imperial-era operational signatures. Clovis teaches Brann smuggler-style false-flag patterns.

side_content.title: First off-world engagement
side_content.hook: Kyle takes Clovis, Inya, and Tarsh to chase a lead at a Tion-fringe shadowport. A junior Inquisitor operator is encountered. Inya takes a wound.

side_content.title: Cassen's family holocomms
side_content.hook: Brann flags Cassen's outgoing holocomms to House Vell as suspicious. The pattern looks like an inside source's reporting. It is not. Cassen will need to be cleared quietly.

side_content.title: Vesh and the senate transcripts
side_content.hook: Vesh receives Senate transcripts at meals from her mother's office. The pattern looks like motive. It is not.

side_content.title: Tarsh repairs the comm array
side_content.hook: The academy's comm array degrades under stress. Tarsh and Clovis spend a day working on it together. Tarsh hums an old freighter song. Clovis recognizes the tune.

side_content.title: Iila wounded â€” perimeter snatch attempt
side_content.hook: The pinch point. A younger student is targeted. Iila intervenes. She is wounded â€” recovering, but the cohort's heart is no longer untouched.

side_content.title: Lirah at the medbay
side_content.hook: Lirah field-medics Iila alongside Cilghal. Cilghal watches Lirah's hands and asks her, quietly, when she stopped letting the work cost her openly.

side_content.title: Joran helping too well
side_content.hook: Joran is everywhere useful. The help is real. Brann notices it is also exactly what an embedded source would do.

side_content.title: Rann tells Clovis what she has been waiting to say
side_content.hook: Rann finds Clovis alone in the colonnade at midnight. Says: 'Something is wrong. I do not know what. I wanted to say it to someone who would not need a reason yet.' Does not name Joran.

side_content.title: A letter from far away
side_content.hook: Mid-act. A letter from Lirah's left-behind partner arrives at the supply shuttle's mail. Lirah does not open it for three days.

side_content.title: Olm finds something he should mention
side_content.hook: Olm finds, in his hereditary papers, a fragment that references a 'Sadow vault' and a counter-ritual. Has not told Tionne.

side_content.title: Kyle proposes an off-world mission
side_content.hook: End of act. Kyle proposes a deeper off-world mission to follow the cell's signature to its operational hub. He wants Clovis. Joran volunteers. Inya wants in.

acts.name: Two Brothers
acts.opening_situation: The off-world mission with Kyle Katarn â€” three days in the Tion fringe, hunting the cell's operational hub. Joran is on the team. The mission produces what Kyle expected: a confrontation with Drel Vass, the cell's senior apprentice. The duel is inconclusive â€” Drel walks away. Returning to Yavin 4, the pieces fit. The inside source is in the cohort. The accumulated evidence narrows the suspect pool. By mid-act, Clovis and Brann have eliminated Cassen and Vesh and arrived at Joran. Clovis follows Joran one night to the lower Massassi corridors â€” the Sith ground under the Praxeum, where Joran has been making his dead drops â€” and the confrontation happens. Joran does not collapse. He has been preparing for this conversation for weeks. He confesses factually, defends the Custodian possessively, refuses the binary as a current demand, and reveals his own divided heart. Then words run out. A duel in Massassi corridor light â€” not training sabers, real sabers, but not to kill. A duel that is each fighter trying to give the other a reason to be different than they are. The duel ends with a position, not a winner. Joran walks back to his dormitory. The protagonist returns to his own bunk. Doubt has been seeded â€” but Joran has not been turned, and will not be turned in a single conversation. What Clovis does with what he now knows is the campaign's central decision. The act closes with that choice. Time skip follows: six weeks of the academy continuing under whatever surface posture the protagonist chose.
acts.opening_location: Tion-fringe shadowport â€” off-world mission staging area
acts.galactic_context: Senator Karro's oversight hearing approaches. Pellaeon's faction sends a deniable diplomatic feeler toward the New Republic â€” not peace yet, but enough to make the Senate cautious. Karrde's network notes the timing as opportunistic. Mara Jade has been recalled to coordinate with Karrde directly. The Disciples of Ragnos's surviving caches are showing up on fringe black markets in patterns Karrde finds suspicious.

side_content.title: Drel Vass â€” first encounter
side_content.hook: On the off-world mission, the cohort tracks the cell's operational hub. Drel Vass is there. The duel happens. Inconclusive. Drel walks away saying three sentences that are not what either Inya or Clovis expected.

side_content.title: Kyle's off-world mentoring
side_content.hook: Three days in close quarters with Kyle. He tells Clovis one story about his own merc-to-Jedi transition â€” the version Luke does not know.

side_content.title: Inya on the south terrace at midnight
side_content.hook: Returning from the off-world mission, Inya cannot sleep. Clovis finds her on the south terrace running her father's drills perfectly. She tells him her father would have lost too, probably.

side_content.title: Cassen's private moment
side_content.hook: Once Cassen is cleared, he and Clovis spend an evening together in the colonnade. Cassen tells Clovis what the family holocomms actually cost him. Shows him the Pantoran devotional bracelet kept hidden in his bunk.

side_content.title: Vesh argues with Clovis privately
side_content.hook: Vesh corners Clovis after sparring and demands to know why he and Brann suspected her. The argument becomes a confession â€” Vesh's father, the way Republic mythology has shaped her grief.

side_content.title: Rann tells Clovis what she has been waiting to say
side_content.hook: Rann finds Clovis after the off-world mission and tells him she has been verifying her hopes about Joran since he arrived, and the floor has not stopped feeling wrong.

side_content.title: Olm finds Tionne in the archive
side_content.hook: Olm comes forward â€” finally â€” with what his family kept. Tionne weeps once. Asks to learn. The counter-knowledge surfaces.

side_content.title: Lirah opens the letter
side_content.hook: Lirah opens the letter from her partner. Does not tell the cohort what it says for two days. When she does, it is to Clovis only, in the kitchen at dawn.

side_content.title: Tev's contact mentions Berris
side_content.hook: An incidental message routed through Karrde's network mentions Berris â€” alive, recovered, asking after Tarsh. Tarsh hears it from Clovis.

side_content.title: The lower Massassi corridors
side_content.hook: Clovis follows Joran to the lower corridors â€” the Sith ground under the Praxeum. The confrontation. The confession. The duel. Doubt seeded; conversion refused.

side_content.title: Telling Rann (or not)
side_content.hook: After the confrontation, Clovis decides whether to tell Rann what he knows. Each option is its own scene. None is clean.

side_content.title: An audience with Luke
side_content.hook: Luke is back from the Senate hearing and takes a quiet evening to ask Clovis how he is doing. Luke knows something is wrong. He does not press.

side_content.title: Kyp offers the resistance meditation
side_content.hook: Kyp Durron offers Clovis the meditation Luke taught him after Carida â€” the one about looking at the worst thing you have done without flinching.

side_content.title: Iila after recovery
side_content.hook: Iila is back in the cohort, the brightness intact but visibly costlier. She finds Clovis and asks, with terrifying clarity, whether he is going to be all right.

time_skip_after.narrative_framing: Six weeks pass at the Praxeum under whatever surface posture the protagonist chose. Joran is now turned, captive, absent, or active â€” and the academy's daily life proceeds around the chosen reality. Senator Karro's hearing has been delayed by political maneuvering and Remnant-facing caution. Pellaeon's faction has gone unusually quiet, which makes Thane's private-cell activity harder to classify. Karrde sends a single coded greeting that contains no questions. The Custodian's cell is preparing the heist.

acts.name: The Custodian's Hand
acts.opening_situation: The time skip ends. The cell's plan accelerates. The heist of the Sadow-line holocron fragment from Tionne's restricted crate is attempted â€” the specifics depend on Joran's posture (active spy: heist hits hard with insider help; absent: heist hits messily with Sona forced into Joran's role; turned: heist is intercepted but Joran's intel was already old; captive: academy is forewarned and Tionne has moved the fragment preemptively, but the cell pivots to direct assault). Whatever the variant, the cohort defends. Brann recognizes Captain Thane's operational signature on the perimeter. The second pinch point is Brann's last stand â€” likely fatal. Olm's counter-knowledge surfaces. Tionne names what she has been afraid to finish translating for five years. Cassen refuses a family extraction order and stays. Vesh finds Rann in the colonnade and tells her three things she was right about. Lirah's anger surfaces openly during triage. Mid-act, Clovis returns to the Glass Wake â€” the Wake reunion turn â€” and then to Karrde for the field log. Karrde's price is agreed. Mara Jade is dispatched. The second plot point is Clovis's return to the Praxeum with the Maradun coordinates. After this, no new information enters the campaign. The cohort prepares for the war-temple.
acts.opening_location: Jedi Praxeum â€” six weeks after the Act 3 confrontation
acts.galactic_context: Senator Karro's hearing has been quietly delayed by Remnant-facing Senate caution and New Republic infighting. The academy's political cover is at its weakest. Karrde's Wild Karrde is positioned at jump distance from Yavin. Mara is dispatched to the Praxeum as Karrde's courier and observer.

side_content.title: The archive breach
side_content.hook: The cell breaches the archive. Tionne fights in the only way she knows how â€” she hides what matters and surrenders what doesn't.

side_content.title: Brann holds the perimeter
side_content.hook: Brann recognizes Captain Thane's operational template. Holds the perimeter against superior force long enough for the cohort to consolidate. The cost is what the cohort feared.

side_content.title: Olm and Tionne in the archive's back room
side_content.hook: Olm walks Tionne through every fragment his family kept. The scene is quiet, slow, and the tactical position changes by the end of it.

side_content.title: Cassen refuses the extraction shuttle
side_content.hook: House Vell sends a private shuttle to extract Cassen during the crisis. Cassen turns it away.

side_content.title: Vesh finds Rann in the colonnade
side_content.hook: Vesh tells Rann three things Rann was right about. Does not apologize. Does not need to. The friendship is real now.

side_content.title: Lirah at triage
side_content.hook: Lirah works triage during the heist defense. The anger is finally undisguised. Cilghal asks her to come to the medbay later for a real conversation. Lirah, this time, says yes.

side_content.title: Tarsh holds the infrastructure
side_content.hook: The academy's power systems take damage during the breach. Tarsh is mechanically critical â€” the academy stays habitable because of him. He hums the whole time.

side_content.title: Iila with the younger students
side_content.hook: During the defense, the younger students cluster around Iila. She gives them small jobs. None of them get hurt.

side_content.title: Reunion with Tev
side_content.hook: Clovis returns to the Glass Wake. The contact-code recipient (chosen in Act 1) is asked about by name. Tev reads Clovis. The crew sees Clovis changed.

side_content.title: Karrde's terms
side_content.hook: Aboard the Wild Karrde or at a neutral shadowport. Mara Jade is present. Karrde reads Clovis in thirty seconds. The two-layer price is named.

side_content.title: Mara observing Clovis
side_content.hook: Mara watches Clovis the way she watches everyone â€” efficiently. She speaks once, to confirm the cell's operational signatures match Inquisitorius records she encountered as Hand.

side_content.title: Luke confronts Clovis
side_content.hook: Late in the act, Luke takes Clovis aside. The conversation depends on Joran's posture and on what Clovis has told Luke. The confrontation is calm.

side_content.title: Streen leaves the tower again
side_content.hook: Streen, who almost never leaves the high tower, comes down during the defense. Stands at the entrance to the great hall with his small whittling knife. Says nothing.

side_content.title: Kyp Durron returns from off-world
side_content.hook: Kyp Durron arrives mid-defense, having heard the academy was under threat. Brings two other knights. Joins the perimeter rotation.

side_content.title: The Maradun expedition planning
side_content.hook: End of act. Clovis has returned with the Maradun field log. The expedition is planned. Roles are assigned. The night before departure is its own scene.

acts.name: What Remains
acts.opening_situation: Dawn. The Wild Karrde and a Praxeum-fitted shuttle (the Horizon, refitted for combat over the past six weeks) jump for the Maradun expanse. The cohort, plus Mara, plus Kyle, plus Luke. The pre-resolution lull happens during the jump â€” Clovis sits with one specific cohort member depending on accumulated bonds. The choice of who is loaded. Arrival at the war-temple. The Custodian's cell is in position. Doctor Eilana Threnn is mid-ritual. Drel Vass is in the combat hall. Sona Kress is on the spiral stair. Captain Thane holds the outer perimeter with mercenaries and conscripted defenders. Vornn waits at the threshold to the ritual chamber. Joran's location varies by his posture entering this act. The fight is six parallel battles. The endings emerge in the immediate aftermath â€” branched on accumulated state, the relationship-state with Joran, the final-turn choices, the Custodian's fate, the cohort's survival, and Karrde's claim. The campaign closes â€” with weight, with cost, and with hooks for everything that comes after.
acts.opening_location: Hyperspace transit toward the Maradun expanse â€” Wild Karrde and the refitted Horizon
acts.galactic_context: The New Republic is unaware. Pellaeon's faction is unaware. Karrde knows; Karrde's network knows; Mara knows. The war-temple's awakening, if it succeeds, will be the next decade's problem. If it fails, only Karrde and the academy will know what was averted.

side_content.title: The night before the war-temple
side_content.hook: During hyperspace transit, Clovis sits with one specific cohort member depending on accumulated bonds â€” Lirah, Inya, Rann, Cassen, or Tarsh. Each is a different scene. Each is loaded.

side_content.title: The outer perimeter â€” Thane's defense
side_content.hook: Captain Thane holds the temple's outer perimeter with mercenaries and conscripted defenders. Brann is no longer here. The non-Force fight is brutal.

side_content.title: Inya vs. Drel Vass
side_content.hook: The combat hall. The duel her father trained her for. Form III defensive perfection against her father's tradition. The fight goes long.

side_content.title: Rann vs. Sona Kress
side_content.hook: The spiral stair. Two women fighting for the same brother â€” one by blood, one by jealousy. The fight is ugly. Whoever wins, Joran loses something.

side_content.title: Tionne, Olm, and Eilana â€” the counter-ritual
side_content.hook: The ritual chamber. Tionne and Olm enter with the counter-knowledge. Eilana is mid-awakening. The contest is not a saber-fight; it is the campaign's thematic argument made manifest.

side_content.title: Luke vs. Vornn at the threshold
side_content.hook: Vornn waits at the threshold to the ritual chamber. Speaks first. Names Luke's pedagogical errors with citations and patience. The duel begins.

side_content.title: Clovis and Joran â€” the duel that matters most
side_content.hook: Clovis's role floats based on Joran's posture. The fight against Joran, alongside Joran, or in pursuit of Joran is the campaign's emotional climax.

side_content.title: The awakening clock
side_content.hook: Eilana's ritual proceeds even as the cohort fights. The clock is real. The cohort has minutes, not turns.

side_content.title: Mara at the war-temple
side_content.hook: Mara fights briefly at the war-temple â€” supporting muscle, not a featured presence. Her two scenes confirm the threat was real enough to draw her, and that she will leave before the falling action.

side_content.title: Kyp at the war-temple
side_content.hook: Kyp Durron has come along. He fights without ceremony. Tells Clovis afterward that there will be a morning a year from now where Clovis will think he is over it and will not be over it; Kyp will be in.

side_content.title: Resolution â€” Open Door
side_content.hook: Joran turned at the climax. Vornn defeated. Massassi dormant. Cohort mostly intact. Karrde calls his favor in six months. Clovis becomes a Jedi.

side_content.title: Resolution â€” Long Road
side_content.hook: Joran sabotaged then disappeared. Vornn escapes wounded. Some Massassi partially awakened. Karrde's claim deepened. Luke knows the lie.

side_content.title: Resolution â€” The Law
side_content.hook: Joran captured at confrontation. Vornn killed cleanly by Luke. Massassi fully prevented. Cohort mostly intact. Rann never forgives. Karrde respects but waits years.

side_content.title: Resolution â€” Third Path
side_content.hook: Mid-climax, Clovis chose Rann over the fight. Heavy cohort losses. Clovis and Rann disappear into Karrde's network.

side_content.title: Resolution â€” What Remains
side_content.hook: Player did not commit. Multiple major losses. Vornn escapes wounded. Massassi partially awaken. Joran's fate unresolved. Karrde withdraws interest.

story_architecture.dramatic_premise: A smuggler-raised Force-sensitive arrives at Luke Skywalker's five-year-old Praxeum and forms his first easy friendship with another new arrival â€” a young man named Joran Veska whose warmth is genuine and whose mission is to extract the long-lost sister he has just reunited with, on behalf of the surviving Imperial Inquisitor who raised him from age nine. The protagonist must navigate a friendship he cannot afford to fully believe, a teaching tradition he was never built to receive, and an information-broker (Karrde) who is patiently waiting for him to come back to the life he is trying to leave.
story_architecture.central_dramatic_question: When the friend you trust is also the betrayer you need to stop, when the institution asking for your loyalty has not yet earned it, when the smuggler-life you came from is still offering you a place to land, and when the antagonist's pedagogy is partially correct about your teacher's blind spots â€” what does belonging actually mean, and what are you willing to lose to claim it?
story_architecture.story_promise: A journey from arrival-as-outsider through accumulated belonging through unwanted clarity to a choice that costs something real. Joran's story is the campaign's emotional spine: he cannot be saved by a single confrontation, and the doubt the protagonist plants either blooms in the climax or does not. Five distinct endings, none clean. Three carry forward into the planned saga layer.
story_architecture.antagonistic_force: Vornn â€” a surviving Imperial Inquisitor of the artifact-retrieval branch, who served Palpatine while quietly concluding that Palpatine was using Sith heritage incorrectly, who has spent twenty years teaching his apprentice (Joran) the corrected Inquisitorius pedagogy he believes the Empire abandoned, and who now intends to use the Sadow-line holocron fragment in Tionne's restricted archive to awaken a Massassi sister-site and establish a private domain in the Maradun expanse. Vornn is not Sith. Vornn loves Joran. Vornn is partially correct about the Praxeum's pedagogical thinness. Vornn's judgment has been compromised by twenty years of Sith primary-source exposure in ways he reads as enlightenment. He is the antagonist of the story Luke is telling himself about the academy, not the antagonist of the player's individual virtue.
story_architecture.thematic_throughline: Belonging is not where you came from â€” it is where you have chosen, with witnesses, to make yourself indispensable. The institution can fail you and still be worth defending. The friend who betrays you can love you and still need to be stopped. The work is choosing what caution serves.
story_architecture.ending_payoff_sketch: Five distinct endings selected by the relationship-state with Joran entering Act 5 + accumulated bond events + final-turn choices at the war-temple convergence. Open Door / Long Road / The Law / Third Path / What Remains. No ending is clean. Four carry forward into the saga layer.

era_voice.era: New Republic â€” Praxeum Maturation Period
era_voice.voice_notes: The galaxy has been breathing for twelve years. The New Republic governs the core and much of the Mid Rim; Pellaeon's consolidated Imperial Remnant controls fortified Outer Rim sectors in disciplined opposition and is still three years from treaty peace. Luke Skywalker's Praxeum at Yavin 4 is no longer the fragile new thing it was during the 11 ABY founding crisis â€” it is five years old, with thirty students, a multi-tiered curriculum, a small senior staff, and the political attention of a Senate oversight coalition. The Exar Kun crisis is five years past. The Disciples of Ragnos crisis is two years past. Brakiss has been operating quietly in the Outer Rim for four years. Mara Jade studies the Force intermittently in Luke and Kyle's orbit and operates with Karrde the rest of the time. The mood is institutional in a way the original founding was not â€” and the institution has begun to discover its compromises before it has fully named them. TONE NOTE â€” this campaign is permitted, and encouraged, to be edgier than typical Praxeum-era fiction. People the protagonist loves can die. The academy can fall. The antagonist's argument must be hard to refute. There is no clean ending.
